close_intro: Compares the document you are writing with texts you already hold: papers on your Reading shelf, your other documents, and any passage you paste in. It marks every run of words that matches a source word for word, and says where. Everything happens in this browser. Nothing is sent anywhere, and no AI is used.
close_cannot_body: It sees only the sources you tick or paste. It does not search the web, books or journals you have not loaded, and it cannot see an idea reused in new words. Use it to catch a paraphrase that hugs a paper you read. It is not a plagiarism verdict, and it is not a similarity report for your institution.
close_shelf_empty: Your Reading shelf is empty. Add papers there, or paste a passage below.
close_paste_label: Or paste a passage to compare with (for example text from a website or a book)
close_doc_locked: Your document is locked. Unlock your vault with the pill at the top, then check again.
close_need_words: Write at least about 30 words first
close_need_source: Tick a source, or paste a passage to compare with
close_failed: The check could not finish. Try again.
close_skipped_one: One ticked paper could not be read and was left out.
close_skipped_many: {n} ticked papers could not be read and were left out.
close_result_rest: ({covered} of {counted} counted) sit inside passages that match your chosen sources word for word, in runs of {minRun} words or more.
close_limits: Quoted text and the reference list were left out. This tool sees only the sources you ticked or pasted. It does not see the web, books, journals you have not loaded, or other students' work, and it cannot see ideas reused in new words. A low number is not a clean bill. A high number is a reason to look again, not proof of anything.
close_none: No passage of {minRun} words or more matched. That is only about the sources you chose.
close_also: The same words also appear in {list}
close_todo: What to do: if these are the author's words, put them in quotation marks with a citation and page, or write the idea again in your own words and cite it.
